newsitem.title: USA: Hearings set on Con Ed steam rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Hearings set on Con Ed steam rate increase.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said it will hold a hearing for public comment on Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's proposal to increase its steam rates beginning October 1, 1997.
As part of a four-year plan, Con Edison has proposed to increase its overall annual revenues from steam service base rates by $16.6 million, or 4.57 percent, the commission said.

The annual revenue increases in the ensuing three years would be 4.4 percent, 4.2 percent and 4.0 percent. The commission said the hearing begins Tuesday, February 18, at 1300 EST/1800 GMT at the commission's offices in New York.
However, the company is proposing revenue allocation and rate design changes that would result in different increases for different categories of customers, the commission said.

For instance, during the first year of the plan, General Service customers would experience a 7.19 percent increase, while rates for Annual Power Service customers would increase by 4.2 percent and rates for Apartment House Service would increase by 4.07 percent.

The company also proposes to implement a weather normalization adjustment applicable to all customers who use steam for space heating during the winter. This would allow the company to adjust monthly bills automatically during wide fluctuations in the weather.

The cimmission said the adjustment is designed to ensure that the company doesn't collect more revenue than expected from customers during extremely cold weather spells when customers might use significantly more steam for heating. Also, the automatic adjustment would ensure that the company continues to collect enough revenue as authorized to cover its costs during much warmer weather when customers might use less steam for heating. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
